subject.title: [Feature Request] Group pairing flow: notify owner + read-only mode for unconfigured groups

question: Should OpenClaw add a shared persisted group-admission lifecycle, and if so, should unapproved group messages be dropped entirely in the first version or may they enter a separately isolated observation path?
rationale: The answer sets the security boundary for untrusted group content, the cross-channel persisted-state model, notification delivery, CLI/API shape, and whether a plugin hook is sufficient or a new core policy contract is needed.

options.title: Stage owner-controlled admission first
options.body: Add pending-group notification plus authorized approve/reject/leave with no pre-approval message delivery or context retention; defer reader mode until its isolation contract is separately reviewed.

options.title: Approve an isolated observation mode
options.body: Define a separate non-replying, non-persistent observation boundary before group admission, with explicit limits on tools, state, transcripts, and owner visibility.

options.title: Keep existing allowlist model
options.body: Retain groupPolicy and channel-specific allowlists without adding group pairing, and direct users to current group configuration and per-channel unknown-group behavior.

recommendation.title: Stage owner-controlled admission first
recommendation.body: Add pending-group notification plus authorized approve/reject/leave with no pre-approval message delivery or context retention; defer reader mode until its isolation contract is separately reviewed.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is the strongest available routing candidate for the shared group-policy, pairing, and channel-access surfaces implicated by the decision.
